nodes.t: A therapy practice near Philadelphia hired me in October to run its website. Everything around it is how I help more people looking for a therapist find them: changes already live, new pages waiting for the owner’s OK, numbers to see what works, and the places people search.
Changes people can see on the site today.
Oct 21 · The map links now open the practice’s Google listing, with reviews, hours and a call button. They used to open a bare street address.

nodes.s: every page has its own title
nodes.t: Oct 28 · Every page is plain readable text with its own title, and the Google description names the right town.
Oct 29 · A link shared in a text or post now shows the office photo and the right page.
Oct 29 · Addresses from earlier versions of the site forward to the current pages, so old links still work.
Oct 29 · The therapists’ bios can be read by search engines and still stay folded until someone taps a card.
Finished and ready to see as previews. Each goes live when the owner says yes.
New home page designs, in three rounds. One was picked on Nov 4 and its full build is in review.
steps: Oct 21 · Four directions, from calm and plain to bold colours.
Oct 27 · Three that combine the favourites. One picked Nov 4.
Nov 5 and 6 · New headline, lighter photos, contact page and footer redone.

nodes.n: Pages for each kind of therapy
nodes.t: One page for each kind of therapy the team offers, written in the words people search, with a plain answer first.
Nov 4 · Articles on questions people search, each with the research behind it on the page.
steps: Nov 2 · The parents sample. Rebuilt Nov 4 around what parents do.
Nov 4 · Leads with when coping skills backfire. 8 sources.
Nov 4 · Why reassurance doesn’t last. 7 sources.
Nov 4 · What the research shows and what is still debated. 10 sources.
Nov 4 · Waves, the five stages, when counseling helps most. 7 sources.

nodes.t: Nov 6 · Two questions (who it’s for, what’s on your mind) lead a visitor to the right articles and pages.
Nov 6 · A plain guide to paying with out-of-network insurance, linked from the fees.
Oct 30 · A one-page sheet for doctors and others who send people to the practice.
How I tell what’s working: a before for everything, every change dated, and the same numbers checked after.
Oct 20 · The site counts when someone sends the form, taps to call or email, or asks for directions. It records only that it happened, never what anyone wrote.

nodes.n: How did you hear about us
nodes.t: Nov 6 · An optional question on the new contact form.
Oct 21 · Which searches show the site and how many people click. Nobody was tracking this before.
Google’s speed score for the home page on a phone: 66 on Oct 26, 73 on Oct 29.
Oct 29 · Every Monday a record rebuilds itself: what changed and what’s waiting.
The places someone looking for a therapist nearby might land.
Oct 19 · Checked the practice’s Google listing and where it shows up on the map.
Nov 3 · The 24 therapy topics people in the area search most, ranked. The new pages and articles come from this list.
Oct 30 · Checked every therapist’s profile on Psychology Today, a directory people use to find therapists, against the site.
Oct 30 · A list of doctors, schools, lawyers and county offices nearby who might send people the practice’s way.
Nov 2 · Where locals look outside Google, like school and parent guides, and which listings have the wrong details.

Nov 9 · For the practice’s booth at a local event, which no one can staff all day: a take-home card with its own tracked QR code, and a card visitors write on and pin to a board. Both were printed by Nov 10. The booth’s signs were already printed with untracked codes, so I set a before to count them by the rise in visits that weekend.

stats: new pages, one per kind of therapy
